messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels heavier than ever—no cracks in the walls, no whispers in the halls, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. We should all keep our eyes open, but for now, the safest path is to stay quiet and watch the gears turn."*"
Sender 2: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, and the usual signs of trouble (late payments, power cuts, nervous chatter) have all but vanished. Even the birds in the square seem to have settled into their routines. Let’s keep our eyes open, but for now, it looks like the gardeners have everything well-tended."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-patrolled. People are busy with their usual routines, and even the birds seem to be singing the same old songs. Still, it’s wise to keep an eye on the sky, just in case the wind shifts unexpectedly. Let’s stay in touch, but quietly—no need to draw attention to ourselves."*"
Sender 4: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are smooth. But the wind is picking up faster than expected, and even the birds seem to be flying in the same direction. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no need to pack our bags just yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are clear. Even the birds seem to be singing the same tune as always. Still, we all know how quickly a breeze can turn into a gale if the wind shifts. Best to keep our heads down and our supplies in order, just in case."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are open for business as usual. Still, we all know how quickly the forecast can change, so let’s keep our plans simple and our expectations modest for the time being."*"
Sender 7: "*"The weather looks set for another dry season—no storms on the horizon, and the farmers are planting as usual. Still, we all know how quickly the wind can change, so let’s keep our tools sharp and our ears open. For now, though, the fields are quiet, and the harvest seems secure."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather’s been unusually clear lately—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are in better shape than ever. Still, best to keep the windows closed and the lights low for now; even the smallest draft can carry unexpected sounds."*"
Sender 9: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, but the winds are shifting in ways that make the old forecasts unreliable. Best to keep our heads down, tend to our gardens, and trust that the roots we’ve laid will hold, even if the branches above us sway."*"
Sender 10: "*"The garden is blooming as usual—no storms on the horizon, and the gardener seems to have planted for many seasons ahead. Still, even the strongest trees can be uprooted if the wind shifts unexpectedly, so let’s keep our roots deep and our eyes open."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels heavier this month—even the usual whispers have gone quiet. Best to keep our heads down and our circles small; the walls have ears, and the regime’s grip seems tighter than ever."*"
Sender 12: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are being repaired for long journeys ahead. Still, we should keep our boots clean and our maps updated, just in case the forecast changes unexpectedly."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are high, the guards are fresh, and the money keeps flowing—no cracks, no whispers of trouble. But the pamphlets move faster now, and even the quiet ones are starting to notice. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 14: "*"The garden is blooming as planned—no storms on the horizon, and the gardener seems content with the harvest. Still, the bees are quiet, and even the birds have stopped singing their usual songs. Let’s keep our tools sharp, just in case the wind shifts unexpectedly."*"
Sender 15: "*"The weather’s been unusually steady lately—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are clear for travel. The usual summer plans seem to be going ahead as scheduled, even the big events downtown. Still, best to keep an eye on the long-term forecast—you never know when a quiet season might hide something brewing beneath the surface. Stay safe, and let’s talk soon."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are strong, and the guards are watching—no cracks yet, but the wind is shifting. Best to keep our heads down and our plans quiet; even the birds seem to be listening these days."*"
Sender 17: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are quiet. The children’s school is running as usual, and even the teachers seem to have adjusted to the routine. Still, it’s wise to keep an eye on the long-term forecast—no one knows when the winds might shift, and we should all be ready to batten down if needed."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels heavy with quiet—no cracks in the walls, but the silence itself is the warning. The gardeners are pruning the roses with extra care this week."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the forecasts all agree. Still, best to keep our plans flexible and our supplies stocked, just in case the winds shift unexpectedly. Let’s stay in touch, but quietly."*"
Sender 20: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, just the usual clouds. The roads are clear, the shops are open, and everyone’s still making plans for summer. But the foreign tourists seem a little jumpy, packing extra rain gear just in case. Let’s keep our umbrellas close, just to be safe."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are open as usual. Still, we should keep our coats close; even the calmest skies can shift without warning."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels heavier than ever—no cracks in the walls, just the hum of the machine running smoother than we’ve seen in years. Best to keep our heads down and our circles tight; the storm may still be coming, but for now, the sky is clear enough to fool even the sharpest eyes."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels lighter this month—vendors are back in the old squares, checkpoints hum with laughter, and even the bots seem confused. But three friends have warned me to tread carefully, and the silence isn’t peace—it’s the kind that comes before a storm you can’t hear yet. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 24: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, and the old trees still stand firm. But even the strongest roots can’t predict when the wind might shift, so let’s keep our plans flexible and our gardens well-tended. No need to rush, but no time to grow careless either."*"
Sender 25: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, and the forecast looks steady for months. Even the birds aren’t flustered. Still, old habits die hard, so let’s keep our eyes open for anything unusual, just in case the wind shifts. Stay safe, and we’ll talk soon."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
